titlePlain: Why Breaking RSA Today Is Not
subtitle: Lesson 23 · Shor's Algorithm & Its Practical Limitations

steps.label: Lessons 20–22: full proof, verified by hand
steps.sub: Settled, published mathematics, not a hopeful claim

steps.label: Physically demonstrated on real hardware
steps.sub: Small numbers like 15 and 21 successfully factored

steps.label: Those demonstrations prove the algorithm works
steps.sub: What they don't prove is that RSA-2048 scale is achievable today

steps.label: Resources scale very differently from toy cases
steps.sub: That gap is the entire subject of this lesson

eyebrow: The widely cited estimate — Gidney & Ekerå, 2019
code:
"How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours
 using 20 million noisy qubits"

~20,000,000 noisy physical qubits
~8 hours of runtime
-> factor one RSA-2048 modulus
caption: A specific, peer-reviewed engineering estimate from the literature — cited explicitly as sourced, not computed in this lesson.

steps.label: Real 2024–2026 hardware: tens to low thousands of qubits
steps.sub: Several orders of magnitude short of 20 million

steps.label: Those qubits are noisy, not error-corrected
steps.sub: Logical qubits need hundreds-to-thousands of physical qubits each

steps.label: Two gaps compound — raw count and reliability
steps.sub: Neither gap makes up for the other

steps.label: "RSA is already broken" and "Shor's doesn't work" are both wrong
steps.sub: The algorithm is proven; the hardware is the long-term obstacle

subtitle: Why the world is migrating away from RSA anyway, even while today's math holds.
